title: Strata
identity: The cataloged Strata is Colin Labadie’s 2012 unaccompanied tenor saxophone work, originally conceived as a solo movement. A 2015 score copy presents Sonder for solo tenor alongside Opia for alto and piano; its program note is internally inconsistent about later planned movements, so the cataloged solo version should remain distinct from the expanded edition.

evidence.claim: The 2015 score copy’s cover identifies Strata for saxophone and piano, with I. Sonder (solo tenor sax) and II. Opia (alto sax and piano); its program note says the piece began as a 2012 solo-tenor work. The score copy is an unidentified user upload on Scribd, not a publisher or composer record.

Visually inspected the score’s transposed solo-tenor opening page and a later passage. Opening has continuous fast repeated-note motion with accents and contrasting f/p dynamics at q=80; later pages retain dense patterned motion. No exact pitch/range claim was taken from the low-resolution preview.

Laura Kerslake’s University of Alberta Doctor of Music thesis (2015), Without Ceasing: A Performance Analysis of Six Solo Works for Saxophone, discusses the 2012 solo-tenor version. Its indexed excerpts identify uninterrupted sixteenth-note texture, circular breathing for most of the work, accented altissimo introduced on score page 2, and wide register leaps; the exact analysis appears around printed pp. 20–21. The university repository copy was not located; accessed only through an uploaded Scribd copy/search index.
evidence.source_name: Laura Kerslake, University of Alberta DMus thesis (2015), third-party Scribd copy

evidence.claim: University of Western Ontario’s 2024–25 saxophone jury requirements list Strata-Opia in upper-level saxophone study and require consultation with the studio teacher for repertoire selection. This supports academic use of the expanded version, not a level for the solo movement.
evidence.source_name: University of Western Ontario saxophone jury requirements

evidence.claim: The 2014 International Jean-Marie Londeix competition repertoire regulation lists Strata for tenor saxophone in its unaccompanied first-elimination round.
evidence.source_name: International Jean-Marie Londeix Saxophone Competition regulations

evidence.claim: Allison Balcetis’s Bandcamp release includes a 7:54 track titled “Strata I. Sonder” by Colin Labadie. This is a verified track listing from the performer’s account; playback was not auditioned.
Composer’s cited strata page was linked by the 2015 score copy and competition listing, but direct access to https://www.colinlabadie.com/strata.html failed.
Sandra Joy Friesen’s performer page documents Bent Note’s 2015 commissioned premiere of Strata-Opia at SaxOpen. This corroborates the distinct saxophone-and-piano version.

score_observations.observation: In the visually inspected transposed tenor-saxophone opening (printed p. 1), a long, tightly repeated rhythmic stream uses written accents and marked contrasting f/p dynamics at q=80. A later inspected solo-tenor page continues the dense repeated-note texture and patterned accents. This is a visual observation from an unofficial, low-resolution third-party copy; exact pitches and range were not recorded.

review_focus: Inference from the inspected transposed score and Kerslake’s indexed analysis: review breath planning for the unbroken pattern, rhythmic steadiness, dynamic separation between accented and non-accented notes, and facility in large register changes/altissimo. The altissimo and circular-breathing claims come from the thesis excerpt, not independent score pitch reading.
collection_flag: Original contemporary solo-tenor saxophone work, documented in an international saxophone competition’s first unaccompanied round and a doctoral performance-analysis project. The separate expanded Strata-Opia edition adds an alto-and-piano movement; do not conflate it with the cataloged solo version.

listening.description: Allison Balcetis’s release lists “Strata I. Sonder” (7:54) by Colin Labadie.
listening.verification: performer-published track listing; playback not auditioned

score_links.description: Third-party upload of the 2015 expanded score; cover and solo-tenor movement opening/later notation visually inspected.

gaps: The composer’s official Strata page and publisher-issued score were not accessible; the notation inspected is an unidentified Scribd user upload.

Original University of Alberta repository copy of Kerslake’s 2015 thesis was not located after focused exact-title, author, and repository searches; pedagogical details remain search-indexed excerpts from a Scribd-hosted copy.
The 2015 score copy has an internally inconsistent program note about the number and sequence of additional movements. Confirm the cataloged version with an authoritative source if possible.
Bandcamp track is identified by the performer and title, but playback and instrument-specific recording details were not auditioned.
